title: Advanced - Darwin's Theory Of Evolution
audio: mp3/151. Advanced - Darwin's Theory Of Evolution.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: We have an advanced lesson for you today.
segments.zh: 我们今天为您提供了高级课程。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: Katrina And my name is Katrin and I'm very excited about this lesson, Marco.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风，我的名字是卡特琳，我对这一课感到非常兴奋，马可。

segments.en: Marco It's very interesting.
segments.zh: 马可这很有趣。

segments.en: It's about a very controversial topic and a very popular person in history, Charles Darwin.
segments.zh: 这是关于一个非常有争议的话题和历史上非常受欢迎的人查尔斯·达尔文。

segments.en: Katrina That's right.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风是对的。

segments.en: So he's most famous perhaps for his book, The Origin of the Species and we're going to be talking a lot about science today.
segments.zh: 所以他最出名的可能是他的书《物种的起源》，我们今天将谈论很多关于科学的事情。

segments.en: So put your thinking caps on.
segments.zh: 所以戴上你的思考帽。

segments.en: Marco Alright, so without further ado, why don't we listen to this dialogue for the first time.
segments.zh: Marco 好吧，所以事不宜迟，我们为什么不第一次听这个对话。

segments.en: Man, it's been forever.
segments.zh: 哥们，好久不见了。

segments.en: What have you been up to lately?
segments.zh: 你最近在做什么？

segments.en: Charles I've been busy preparing for my exams, not to mention all the term papers I've had to write.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 我一直在忙着准备考试，更不用说我必须写的所有学期论文了。

segments.en: Katrina Same here.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜：我也是。

segments.en: I'm up to my neck in work, but at least we've got summer holidays after finals.
segments.zh: 我忙得不可开交，不过好在期末考试后就放暑假了。

segments.en: Where are you headed now?
segments.zh: 你现在要去哪里？

segments.en: Charles I'm going to my anthro class.
segments.zh: 查尔斯：我要去上人类学课。

segments.en: We've been focusing on Darwin all term since it's the 200th anniversary of his birth or whatever.
segments.zh: 这学期我们一直在讲达尔文，好像是因为今年是他诞辰两百周年之类的。

segments.en: I'm sick and tired of Darwin, Darwin, Darwin!
segments.zh: 我厌倦了达尔文、达尔文、达尔文！

segments.en: Katrina What?
segments.zh: 卡特里娜：什么？

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: How can you not like Darwin?
segments.zh: 你怎么能不喜欢达尔文？

segments.en: His work turned thousands of years of ideas about creation on their head.
segments.zh: 他的研究颠覆了人类几千年来对生命起源的认识。

segments.en: His theory of evolution revolutionized the fields of biology and anthropology.
segments.zh: 他的进化论给生物学和人类学带来了革命性变化。

segments.en: Charles I don't like him.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 我不喜欢他。

segments.en: His theory of human evolution and natural selection is full of holes.
segments.zh: 他关于人类进化和自然选择的理论漏洞百出。

segments.en: It's not as solid as you make it out to be.
segments.zh: 它可不像你说的那么站得住脚。

segments.en: Katrina Say that again and you'll make enemies with half of the academy, not to mention your professors.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜：你再这么说，半个学术界都会跟你为敌，更不用说你的教授们了。

segments.en: Furthermore, the explanation proposed by Darwin about the origin of the species and the process of natural selection constitutes a grand step towards a coherent understanding of the world and its very beginnings.
segments.zh: 此外，达尔文对物种起源和自然选择过程提出的解释构成了朝着对世界及其起源的连贯理解迈出的重要一步。

segments.en: Charles I'm not minimizing his huge contributions to science.
segments.zh: 查尔斯：我并没有贬低他对科学的巨大贡献。

segments.en: It's just that his theory reminds me of the conundrum of the chicken and the egg.
segments.zh: 只是他的理论让我想起了鸡和蛋的难题。

segments.en: Katrina What are you talking about?
segments.zh: 卡特里娜：你在说什么？

segments.en: Charles Which came first?
segments.zh: 查尔斯：先有哪个？

segments.en: The chicken or the egg?
segments.zh: 鸡蛋还是鸡蛋？

segments.en: This is a classic logical problem, and I think it applies to Darwin's theory.
segments.zh: 这是一个经典的逻辑问题，我认为它适用于达尔文的理论。

segments.en: How did the very first living organism come to be?
segments.zh: 第一个活的有机体是如何形成的？

segments.en: Katrina Interesting.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜：有意思。

segments.en: I think that question is better suited for my philosophy class.
segments.zh: 我认为这个问题更适合我的哲学课。

segments.en: In the meantime, how about we settle this with a duel?
segments.zh: 与此同时，我们如何通过决斗来解决这个问题？

segments.en: Alright, interesting, they have very different views on Charles Darwin, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，有趣的是，他们对查尔斯·达尔文的看法截然不同，对吧？

segments.en: Katrina They do, and they're both pretty nerdy people.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风，他们都是非常书呆子的人。

segments.en: This is a very nerdy university conversation that's happening between classes.
segments.zh: 这是一场非常书呆子的大学对话，正在课间发生。

segments.en: Charles Yeah, I think maybe they're like PhD candidates or something.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 是的，我想他们可能就像博士候选人之类的。

segments.en: Katrina Perhaps.
segments.zh: 也许是卡特里娜飓风。

segments.en: Alright, so before we get to talking about some of the ideas in today's dialogue, let's talk about some of the words and phrases that we hear to understand better what's going on.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以在我们开始讨论今天对话中的一些想法之前，让我们谈谈我们听到的一些单词和短语，以便更好地理解正在发生的事情。

segments.en: The first part we're going to talk about in today's Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 我们将在今天的语言外卖中讨论的第一部分。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Charles Alright, on Language Takeaway today, let's take a look at the first word.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 好吧，关于今天的语言外卖，让我们来看看第一个词。

segments.en: And well, one of the things that many people say is that Darwin revolutionized the fields of biology.
segments.zh: 好吧，许多人说的一件事是达尔文彻底改变了生物学领域。

segments.en: Katrina And so he revolutionized these because he pushed them forward.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风和所以他彻底改变了这些，因为他推动了它们。

segments.en: He made many changes.
segments.zh: 他做了很多改变。

segments.en: He forced changes.
segments.zh: 他强迫改变。

segments.en: So people had to change the way that they thought about these things.
segments.zh: 所以人们必须改变他们对这些事情的看法。

segments.en: Charles If you revolutionize something, a topic or an idea, you are creating new knowledge almost, right?
segments.zh: 查尔斯，如果你彻底改变了某事、一个话题或一个想法，你几乎是在创造新知识，对吧？

segments.en: Katrina Exactly.
segments.zh: Katrina：没错。

segments.en: You can think of the word revolution, which is a thing.
segments.zh: 你可以想到革命这个词，这是一件事。

segments.en: So you think of the Russian Revolution or the American Revolution.
segments.zh: 所以你想想俄国革命或美国革命。

segments.en: These are times of change.
segments.zh: 这些是变革的时代。

segments.en: So to revolutionize is to bring about change.
segments.zh: 因此，革命化就是带来变革。

segments.en: Charles Very good.
segments.zh: Charles：很好。

segments.en: Alright, so moving forward, they were talking about human evolution.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以向前迈进，他们在谈论人类进化。

segments.en: Human evolution.
segments.zh: 人类进化。

segments.en: What is that exactly?
segments.zh: 那到底是什么？

segments.en: Katrina Good question.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风好问题。

segments.en: So you're not a monkey.
segments.zh: 所以你不是猴子。

segments.en: I'm not a monkey, but we come from monkeys, right?
segments.zh: 我不是猴子，但我们来自猴子，对吧？

segments.en: Charles So we evolved.
segments.zh: 查尔斯，所以我们进化了。

segments.en: Katrina Right.
segments.zh: Katrina：对。

segments.en: So the process is called human evolution.
segments.zh: 所以这个过程被称为人类进化。

segments.en: That means the process by which humans changed forms to become what we are today.
segments.zh: 这意味着人类改变形式以成为我们今天的样子的过程。

segments.en: Charles Okay, so you evolve.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 好的，所以你进化了。

segments.en: Now is it evolution?
segments.zh: 现在是进化吗？

segments.en: You usually think of something positive, right?
segments.zh: 你通常会想到一些积极的东西，对吧？

segments.en: Something evolves into something better.
segments.zh: 某事演变成更好的东西。

segments.en: Is it always that way?
segments.zh: 总是这样吗？

segments.en: Katrina No, we have another word for the negative, right?
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风 不，我们还有另一个词来形容否定，对吧？

segments.en: So the positive is to evolve, to become better.
segments.zh: 所以积极的是进化，变得更好。

segments.en: To get worse is to devolve.
segments.zh: 变得更糟就是下放。

segments.en: Charles Okay.
segments.zh: 查尔斯好吧。

segments.en: Katrina Yeah, to devolve, to go back and to kind of lose things that you had.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风 是的，下放，回去，失去你所拥有的东西。

segments.en: Charles Okay, interesting.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 好吧，有趣。

segments.en: And then they were also talking about Darwin's theory of natural selection.
segments.zh: 然后他们也在谈论达尔文的自然选择理论。

segments.en: Natural selection.
segments.zh: 自然选择。

segments.en: Katrina Okay, this is maybe one of the things that Darwin was most famous for, and that's why we've included it in this language takeaway because it's a key phrase.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风 好吧，这可能是达尔文最著名的事情之一，这就是为什么我们将它包含在这个语言外卖中的原因，因为它是一个关键短语。

segments.en: It's something you hear people talk about a lot.
segments.zh: 这是你听到人们经常谈论的事情。

segments.en: Okay, so natural selection is a process again, and it's the process by which stronger animals survive over time and weaker animals don't.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以自然选择又是一个过程，它是更强壮的动物随着时间的推移而生存而弱小的动物无法生存的过程。

segments.en: So if there's a weak species, it can't really survive because it keeps dying and dying, and then finally there's no more.
segments.zh: 因此，如果有一个弱弱的物种，它就无法真正生存下来，因为它一直在死亡和死亡，然后终于没有了。

segments.en: And so this is called natural selection because no one's actually choosing what animals will survive, but it's kind of a natural process.
segments.zh: 所以这被称为自然选择，因为没有人真正选择可以生存的动物，但这是一个自然的过程。

segments.en: Charles Right, Mother Nature is choosing it.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 对，大自然母亲正在选择它。

segments.en: Katrina Right.
segments.zh: Katrina：对。

segments.en: Charles Very good.
segments.zh: Charles：很好。

segments.en: So natural selection, this is one of the things that Darwin is most famous for.
segments.zh: 所以自然选择，这是达尔文最著名的事情之一。

segments.en: And well, as Katrina mentioned, Darwin wrote the book Origin of the Species.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如卡特里娜飓风所说，达尔文写了《该物种的起源》一书。

segments.en: Katrina Right, so origin means beginning.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风是正确的，所以起源意味着开始。

segments.en: So the origin of mankind, right?
segments.zh: 那么人类的起源，对吧？

segments.en: So there are many different kinds of animals.
segments.zh: 所以有很多种不同的动物。

segments.en: You could even say there are many different kinds of like mammals, but there are many different species within that.
segments.zh: 你甚至可以说有许多不同种类的哺乳动物，但其中有许多不同的物种。

segments.en: So human beings, black bears, koalas, chimpanzees, these are all species.
segments.zh: 所以人类、黑熊、考拉、黑猩猩，这些都是物种。

segments.en: And so a species is a classification.
segments.zh: 所以物种是一种分类。

segments.en: So the origin of the species is kind of a way of telling the story of how all these things came about.
segments.zh: 因此，该物种的起源是一种讲述所有这些事情是如何产生的故事的方式。

segments.en: Charles All right, the origin of the species.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 好吧，物种的起源。

segments.en: And the last one, this word is kind of strange.
segments.zh: 最后一个，这个词有点奇怪。

segments.en: He talked about the conundrum of the chicken and the egg.
segments.zh: 他谈到了鸡和蛋的难题。

segments.en: Katrina Okay, conundrum.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜 好吧，难题。

segments.en: I love this word.
segments.zh: 我喜欢这个词。

segments.en: It's very funny sounding.
segments.zh: 这听起来很有趣。

segments.en: Conundrum.
segments.zh: 难题。

segments.en: It means like a problem or a riddle or something that's hard to understand.
segments.zh: 这意味着像一个问题或一个谜语或难以理解的东西。

segments.en: Charles All right.
segments.zh: 查尔斯好吧。

segments.en: So in this case, it's the conundrum of the chicken and the egg, right, which came first.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，首先出现的是鸡和蛋的难题。

segments.en: How else can you use conundrum?
segments.zh: 你还能如何使用难题？

segments.en: Katrina You could say that maybe there's a situation that's very strange and hard to understand.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风 你可以说，也许有一种非常奇怪和难以理解的情况。

segments.en: This is quite a conundrum.
segments.zh: 这是一个相当难的难题。

segments.en: Charles This is quite a conundrum we have.
segments.zh: 查尔斯这是我们的一个难题。

segments.en: It sounds very fancy, very well educated.
segments.zh: 这听起来很花哨，受过良好的教育。

segments.en: Katrina It does.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风确实如此。

segments.en: Charles All right.
segments.zh: 查尔斯好吧。

segments.en: So interesting words on language takeaway.
segments.zh: 关于语言外卖的有趣词。

segments.en: Why don't we move on now to four phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 为什么我们现在不继续讨论 Fluency Builder 上的四个短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: All right, on Fluency Builder today, we have four phrases as we said.
segments.zh: 好吧，在今天的 Fluency Builder 上，我们有四个短语，正如我们所说。

segments.en: So what's the first one?
segments.zh: 那么第一个是什么？

segments.en: Katrina The first one is great.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风第一个很棒。

segments.en: It's very visual.
segments.zh: 它非常直观。

segments.en: You say, I'm up to my neck in work.
segments.zh: 你说，我在工作中到了我的脖子。

segments.en: I'm up to my neck in papers to write.
segments.zh: 我靠在纸上写。

segments.en: All right, so this means I have so much stuff to do that you could pile it up and it would come up to my neck.
segments.zh: 好吧，这意味着我有很多事情要做，你可以把它堆起来，它会到达我的脖子上。

segments.en: Charles So I have as many papers that are almost as tall as I am.
segments.zh: 查尔斯，所以我的论文几乎和我一样高。

segments.en: Katrina Exactly.
segments.zh: Katrina：没错。

segments.en: And so I could say I'm up to my neck in work.
segments.zh: 所以我可以说我在工作中达到了我的目的。

segments.en: I have no more time to do anything.
segments.zh: 我没有更多的时间做任何事情。

segments.en: Charles Sometimes people also say I'm up to here and then they'll like, they'll point at their forehead or somewhere around their head.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 有时人们也会说我到这里，然后他们会喜欢，他们会指向他们的额头或头部周围的某个地方。

segments.en: I'm up to here with your nonsense.
segments.zh: 我在这里说你的废话。

segments.en: Katrina Exactly.
segments.zh: Katrina：没错。

segments.en: So this is a way of saying that I'm really busy.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种说我真的很忙的方式。

segments.en: Charles Really busy.
segments.zh: 查尔斯真的很忙。

segments.en: I'm really tired of it.
segments.zh: 我真的厌倦了。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And our next phrase is one that most mothers use.
segments.zh: 我们的下一个短语是大多数母亲使用的短语。

segments.en: I'm sick and tired.
segments.zh: 我病了也很累。

segments.en: Katrina I'm sick and tired of all of your whining.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风 我厌倦了你所有的抱怨。

segments.en: Go do the dishes and don't complain.
segments.zh: 去洗碗，不要抱怨。

segments.en: Charles Right.
segments.zh: Charles：对。

segments.en: So it's always, it always goes together.
segments.zh: 所以它总是，它总是在一起。

segments.en: You are sick and tired.
segments.zh: 你病了也很累。

segments.en: Katrina Right.
segments.zh: Katrina：对。

segments.en: And sick comes first.
segments.zh: 生病是第一位的。

segments.en: So I'm sick and tired of this.
segments.zh: 所以我厌倦了这个。

segments.en: I'm sick and tired of your bad attitude.
segments.zh: 我厌倦了你的坏态度。

segments.en: Charles Okay.
segments.zh: 查尔斯好吧。

segments.en: So and that means that you are...
segments.zh: 所以，这意味着你是...

segments.en: Katrina I'm just tired of it.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风我只是厌倦了它。

segments.en: I don't want you to have a bad attitude anymore.
segments.zh: 我不想让你的态度不好了。

segments.en: I'm just, yeah.
segments.zh: 我只是，是的。

segments.en: Charles I'm really annoyed by it.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 我真的很生气。

segments.en: I'm annoyed.
segments.zh: 我很生气。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Sick and tired.
segments.zh: 生病和疲倦。

segments.en: And then we saw a phrase that was a little bit separated.
segments.zh: 然后我们看到了一个有点分开的短语。

segments.en: He said the sentence went like this.
segments.zh: 他说这句话是这样的。

segments.en: His work turned thousands of years of ideas about creation on their head.
segments.zh: 他的研究颠覆了人类几千年来对生命起源的认识。

segments.en: So to turn something on its head.
segments.zh: 所以要把某事转到头上。

segments.en: Katrina Like you said, Marco, it's split into two parts.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风就像你说的，马可，它分为两部分。

segments.en: So he turned the field of computer science on its head.
segments.zh: 于是，他把计算机科学领域颠覆了。

segments.en: So to turn on its head means to completely reverse something, to turn it around.
segments.zh: 因此，打开它的头意味着完全颠倒某物，将其扭转。

segments.en: You think 180 degrees.
segments.zh: 你以为180度。

segments.en: And so if biology used to be one way, then Darwin made it completely different.
segments.zh: 因此，如果生物学曾经是一种方式，那么达尔文让它完全不同。

segments.en: Charles So we can say that Isaac Newton completely turned physics on its head with his theory or his findings on gravity.
segments.zh: 查尔斯 所以我们可以说艾萨克·牛顿用他的理论或他关于引力的发现完全颠覆了物理学的头脑。

segments.en: Katrina And then years and years later, we had Albert Einstein who turned those theories or who turned that theory on its head with his own ideas about physics.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风，然后多年后，我们有阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦，他将这些理论转向了这些理论，或者他用自己对物理学的想法颠覆了这个理论。

segments.en: Charles Very good.
segments.zh: Charles：很好。

segments.en: So to turn something on its head, to completely change the course of or prove something to be maybe wrong.
segments.zh: 因此，要颠覆某事，彻底改变或证明某事可能是错误的。

segments.en: And the last phrase that we have is the person argued that Darwin's theories were full of holes.
segments.zh: 我们的最后一句话是那个人认为达尔文的理论充满了漏洞。

segments.en: Katrina Okay.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜 好吧。

segments.en: So to say a theory is full of holes is a little bit different than saying that his pants are full of holes.
segments.zh: 所以说一个理论充满了洞，与说他的裤子里满是洞有点不同。

segments.en: Because when you say something is full of holes, maybe they actually have holes.
segments.zh: 因为当你说某事充满了洞时，也许他们实际上有洞。

segments.en: But a theory is it's an idea.
segments.zh: 但一个理论是它是一个想法。

segments.en: So it can't have holes.
segments.zh: 所以它不能有洞。

segments.en: What you're saying is that it's not completely sound.
segments.zh: 你说的是它并不完全正确。

segments.en: It's not without some problems.
segments.zh: 它并非没有一些问题。

segments.en: And so maybe you're saying that, well, the cookies are gone out of the kitchen, Marco.
segments.zh: 所以也许你是在说，好吧，饼干已经从厨房里消失了，马可。

segments.en: And I saw you in the kitchen.
segments.zh: 我在厨房看到你。

segments.en: So clearly you ate the cookies.
segments.zh: 很明显，你吃了饼干。

segments.en: Charles Right.
segments.zh: Charles：对。

segments.en: So I can say that's full of holes because it was me and it was three other people who were in the kitchen.
segments.zh: 所以我可以说那是满是洞，因为是我，还有另外三个人在厨房里。

segments.en: So you can't blame me.
segments.zh: 所以你不能怪我。

segments.en: Katrina Ah, it could have been the other two people.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜啊，可能是另外两个人。

segments.en: Charles Right.
segments.zh: Charles：对。

segments.en: So if something is full of holes, it's that it has maybe mistakes or it's still missing complete evidence to prove it right.
segments.zh: 因此，如果某些东西充满了洞，那就是它可能有错误，或者它仍然缺少完整的证据来证明它是正确的。

segments.en: Katrina Or it has bad logic.
segments.zh: 卡特里娜飓风或它的逻辑不好。

segments.en: Charles Bad logic.
segments.zh: 查尔斯糟糕的逻辑。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: So we've taken a look at a lot of words and different phrases here.
segments.zh: 所以我们在这里看了很多单词和不同的短语。

segments.en: Let's listen to this argument one last time.
segments.zh: 让我们最后一次听这个论点。

segments.en: Man, it's been forever.
segments.zh: 伙计，这是永远的。

segments.en: What have you been up to lately?
segments.zh: 你最近在做什么？

segments.en: I've been busy preparing for my exams, not to mention all the term papers I've had to write.
segments.zh: 我一直在忙着准备考试，更不用说我必须写的所有学期论文了。

segments.en: Same here.
segments.zh: 我也是。

segments.en: I'm up to my neck in work, but at least we've got summer holidays after finals.
segments.zh: 我忙得不可开交，不过好在期末考试后就放暑假了。

segments.en: Where are you headed now?
segments.zh: 你现在要去哪里？

segments.en: I'm going to my anthro class.
segments.zh: 我要去我的人类课。

segments.en: We've been focusing on Darwin all term since it's the 200th anniversary of his birth or whatever.
segments.zh: 这学期我们一直在讲达尔文，好像是因为今年是他诞辰两百周年之类的。

segments.en: I'm sick and tired of Darwin, Darwin, Darwin.
segments.zh: 我厌倦了达尔文、达尔文、达尔文。

segments.en: What?
segments.zh: 什么？

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: How can you not like Darwin?
segments.zh: 你怎么能不喜欢达尔文？

segments.en: His work turned thousands of years of ideas about creation on their head.
segments.zh: 他的研究颠覆了人类几千年来对生命起源的认识。

segments.en: His theory of evolution revolutionized the fields of biology and anthropology.
segments.zh: 他的进化论给生物学和人类学带来了革命性变化。

segments.en: I don't like him.
segments.zh: 我不喜欢他。

segments.en: His theory of human evolution and natural selection is full of holes.
segments.zh: 他关于人类进化和自然选择的理论漏洞百出。

segments.en: It's not as solid as you make it out to be.
segments.zh: 它可不像你说的那么站得住脚。

segments.en: Say that again and you'll make enemies with half of the academy, not to mention your professors.
segments.zh: 再说一遍，你会和学院的一半人结为敌人，更不用说你的教授了。

segments.en: Furthermore, the explanation proposed by Darwin about the origin of the species and the process of natural selection constitutes a grand step towards a coherent understanding of the world and its very beginnings.
segments.zh: 此外，达尔文对物种起源和自然选择过程提出的解释构成了朝着对世界及其起源的连贯理解迈出的重要一步。

segments.en: I'm not minimizing his huge contributions to science.
segments.zh: 我没有尽量减少他对科学的巨大贡献。

segments.en: It's just that his theory reminds me of the conundrum of the chicken and the egg.
segments.zh: 只是他的理论让我想起了鸡和蛋的难题。

segments.en: What are you talking about?
segments.zh: 你在说什么？

segments.en: Which came first, the chicken or the egg?
segments.zh: 哪个先来，鸡还是蛋？

segments.en: This is a classic logical problem and I think it applies to Darwin's theory.
segments.zh: 这是一个经典的逻辑问题，我认为它适用于达尔文的理论。

segments.en: How did the very first living organism come to be?
segments.zh: 第一个活的有机体是如何形成的？

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: I think that question is better suited for my philosophy class.
segments.zh: 我认为这个问题更适合我的哲学课。

segments.en: In the meantime, how about we settle this with a duel?
segments.zh: 与此同时，我们如何通过决斗来解决这个问题？

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: It's interesting, Darwin's theories and his explanations for the origin of species and life as we know it.
segments.zh: 这很有趣，达尔文的理论以及他对我们所知道的物种和生命起源的解释。

segments.en: But there is the opposite to this, right?
segments.zh: 但这与此相反，对吧？

segments.en: There is a certain thing called creationism.
segments.zh: 有一种东西叫做创造论。

segments.en: There is and this is a big source of controversy, especially in the United States because in some places people want to teach creationism as well as evolution in schools.
segments.zh: 有一个很大的争议来源，尤其是在美国，因为在某些地方，人们想要教授创造论和学校的进化论。

segments.en: So this is the big question.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个大问题。

segments.en: Are they still equal as theories or is one theory more proven than the other?
segments.zh: 它们是否仍然与理论相等，还是一种理论比另一种理论更被证明？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And it is kind of hard to determine which one is better because one is based on faith, the other one is based more on scientific evidence, right?
segments.zh: 很难确定哪一种更好，因为一种是基于信仰，另一种更多基于科学证据，对吧？

segments.en: So they're not really even on the same scale as we learned before.
segments.zh: 因此，它们的规模甚至不像我们之前学到的那样。

segments.en: That's kind of like apples and oranges, right?
segments.zh: 这有点像苹果和橙子，对吧？

segments.en: It is and there are some people who would say that we have lots of ways of quote unquote proving what happened in the past but as long as we weren't there, we never really do know.
segments.zh: 确实是，有些人会说我们有很多方法可以引用过去发生的事情来证明过去发生的事情，但只要我们不在那里，我们就永远不会真正知道。

segments.en: And there's always changes in science so how can we be sure that what we know now isn't false, isn't misunderstanding.
segments.zh: 科学总是有变化，所以我们如何确定我们现在所知道的不是错误的，不是误解。

segments.en: I think for now, this is the best explanation but that doesn't mean that it's the correct one.
segments.zh: 我认为，这是最好的解释，但这并不意味着它是正确的。

segments.en: Maybe in a hundred years from now, we'll have another explanation that's much better or maybe complementary to this one.
segments.zh: 也许在一百年后，我们将有另一种更好的解释，或者可能与这个相辅相成。

segments.en: So we want to know what you guys think, come to our website englishpod.com.
segments.zh: 所以我们想知道你们的想法，来我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: We really want to hear your opinions.
segments.zh: 我们真的很想听听您的意见。

segments.en: What do you think about this topic?
segments.zh: 你对这个话题有什么看法？

segments.en: It is a little bit controversial so we really look forward to your comments and any other questions you may have.
segments.zh: 这有点争议，所以我们非常期待您的评论和您可能有的任何其他问题。

segments.en: Yep.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And just a reference, creationism is the idea that God created the world or a superior being created the world and that everything came from that.
segments.zh: 只是一个参考，神创论是上帝创造了世界或一个优越的存在创造了世界的想法，并且一切都来自于此。

segments.en: And so let us know what you think.
segments.zh: 所以让我们知道你的想法。

segments.en: I am very curious too and that's about it for today.
segments.zh: 我也很好奇，这就是今天。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 到时候在那里见。

segments.en: You're taking off for a walk.
segments.zh: 你要起飞去散步。
